clue.text: Training run and jog Ben has in city

indicators.note: training puts the body through drills and reshaping, so the letters that follow are put through a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A man called Ben fits a training run and a jog into his day while staying in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of RUN plus JOG BEN HAS are rearranged; 'and' only joins the two pieces of fodder, and 'in' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannesburg is the largest city in South Africa, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Spear, article Indonesian discards before river rises

indicators.note: before places the trimmed Indonesian ahead of the river in the answer
to discard is to throw away, so the article's letters are thrown out of the Indonesian

parts.note: a Javan is a native of Java, the main island of Indonesia
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the river's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Nile is the great river of Egypt

explanation.surface: An Indonesian man throws aside a piece of writing before the river floods, spear in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: JAVAN loses AN to give JAV; NILE written upwards gives ELIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A javelin is a light spear thrown by hand, in war or in athletics.

clue.text: One kept prisoner for 18 years under army

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the years below the army in the answer

parts.note: a host is a large army or multitude, as in the heavenly host
eighteen is the age of majority, when one comes of age, so the years are an age

explanation.surface: Someone is held captive by soldiers for eighteen years.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person seized and detained as security for a demand being met.

clue.text: Am insured to cook for nanny

indicators.note: to cook figures or accounts is to tamper with them, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says they have insurance so that they can cook for the family's nanny.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after children, the same job as a nanny.

clue.text: Moral belief within Elizabeth I consistently

indicators.note: within says the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows, across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Queen Elizabeth I held one firm moral principle all her life.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a principle of right conduct, a moral conviction a person holds.

clue.text: Tortilla dish, whisper love eating it

indicators.note: eating means the outer pieces take the word it inside them

parts.note: a burr is a soft whirring or rough murmuring sound, a kind of whisper
love is nil in tennis, written as the round letter O

explanation.surface: A lover murmurs sweet nothings while eating a Mexican wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrito is a Mexican dish of a flour tortilla rolled round a filling of beans or meat.

clue.text: Son leaves showing calm acceptance, having prevailed

indicators.note: leaves means the son's letter departs from the longer word

parts.note: someone resigned to fate accepts it calmly
S is the standard abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A son walks out, calmly accepting that someone else has won the argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to hold sway or be predominant, so to have prevailed is to have reigned.

clue.text: Good enough outside, it's a fantastic small plant

indicators.note: outside says the small plant wraps round the shuffled letters

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
a plant is a factory or works

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters of it's a are reworked

explanation.surface: A tiny plant growing outdoors is judged good enough, even fantastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' looks like praise for the plant but signals the anagram of IT'S A (giving ATIS), and 'outside' says the small plant wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfactory means adequate, meeting a standard without being outstanding.

clue.text: Consultant, regularly paid, avoids worry

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth, sixth and so on

explanation.surface: A consultant who is paid on a regular basis no longer has money worries.
explanation.definitionFit: An adviser, also spelt with -or, is someone consulted for expert guidance, a consultant.

clue.text: Somewhat difficult mess engulfing River Police officer

indicators.note: engulfing means the mess swallows the river and officer

parts.note: to make a hash of something is to make a mess of it
R is the map abbreviation for river
DI is Detective Inspector, a British police rank

explanation.surface: A river police officer is caught up in a rather tricky mess.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish softens an adjective, so this means fairly hard, rather tough.

clue.text: Occupation accustomed to everyday shocks and sometimes severe cutbacks?

definitions.text: Occupation accustomed to everyday shocks and sometimes severe cutbacks?

parts.words: Occupation accustomed to everyday shocks and sometimes severe cutbacks?
parts.note: shocks are thick masses of hair and cutbacks are haircuts, so this is the trade of the salon stylist, disguised as a business suffering hard times

explanation.surface: A beleaguered profession endures daily upsets and occasional brutal budget cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'shocks' as heads of hair and 'cutbacks' as trims at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Styling and cutting hair is a trade whose daily material is shocks of hair and whose work is cutting it back.

clue.text: Sick notes in disrepute

parts.note: to be ill is to be sick
fa and me (also mi) are notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Sick notes have fallen into disrepute.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill fame is a bad reputation, as in a house of ill fame, so it means disrepute.

clue.text: Overheard legend resisting wine

indicators.note: overheard says the word for legend is caught by ear and spelt differently

parts.note: the legend on a map is its key, explaining the symbols
anti means opposed to, resisting

explanation.surface: A legendary figure is overheard refusing a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian CHI is said like 'key'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany in Italy.

clue.text: Guard criminal

definitions.meaning: a barrier round a field or garden that protects or encloses it
in slang, a dealer who receives and sells stolen goods

explanation.surface: A security guard turns out to be a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is both a protective barrier and a receiver of stolen property.

clue.text: A second prisoner departs, having stuffed sack and escaped

indicators.note: having stuffed means these letters are packed inside the sack

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed, as in hitting the sack
S is the abbreviation for second, as in units of time
a con is a convict, a prisoner
D stands for departs on timetables

explanation.surface: A convict leaves after a moment, having filled a sack with loot and fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having stuffed' reads as a burglar filling a bag, but it signals the container: the sack is filled with the second, prisoner and departs abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to leave secretly, often to evade the law, so it means escaped.

clue.text: Coat perhaps keeps flashing inside leg area

indicators.note: inside places the shuffled letters within the leg area

parts.note: the shin is the front of the lower leg

indicators.note: flashing suggests quick, jumbled movement, so the letters of keeps are rearranged

explanation.surface: A flasher keeps exposing parts of the leg under a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flashing' suggests indecent exposure, but it signals the anagram of keeps (giving EEPSK), which 'inside' sets within the leg area.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepskin is a garment made from a sheep's hide with fleece on; a coat is one example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Game's copyright superseding patent, initially it carries charge

indicators.note: superseding means one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: partridge is a game bird, shot for sport and the table

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of patent

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for copyright, as in the circled symbol

explanation.surface: A game's copyright overrides a patent, holding the charge.
explanation.walkthrough: In PARTRIDGE the P is replaced by C.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartridge is a case holding a bullet and its explosive charge.

clue.text: Ceremonial emblems Algeria reforms

indicators.note: reforms means the letters of the country are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Algeria overhauls the symbols of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the insignia of royalty or office, such as crowns and sceptres.

clue.text: Lintels beginning to go for extortionate prices

indicators.note: beginning to go means the first letter departs

parts.note: a transom is a horizontal crossbar above a door or window, a lintel

explanation.surface: Builders charge outrageous sums for the beams over doors.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is a price demanded for a captive's release, an extortionate sum.

clue.text: First sign of parish notice about priest

indicators.note: first sign of means only the opening letter of parish

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a notice
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A parish notice mentions the priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is a military chaplain or informal word for a priest.

clue.text: It's not designed to cure home with unpleasant smell

parts.note: one's place is one's home, as in come round to my place
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A smelly house cannot be fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy pill with no active ingredient, given for its psychological effect rather than to heal.

clue.text: Makes twice as many shots in snooker?

definitions.meaning: in snooker a double is a shot that rebounds off a cushion into a pocket; the question mark flags this example

explanation.surface: A snooker player takes twice as many shots as the opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for multiplying by two and the plural of a snooker shot played off a cushion.

clue.text: Sheer material in newspaper attracting unknown journalists essentially

indicators.note: attracting draws the following letters onto the end of the newspaper

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or periodical that speaks for a group
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

indicators.note: essentially means the very centre, the middle letter of journalists

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on sheer fabric draws in mysterious journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: Organza is a thin, stiff, see-through fabric of silk or synthetic fibre.

clue.text: Tea service close to grandma getting knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over, in a down clue, means the letters are upended and read from the bottom

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of grandma

explanation.surface: A tea service near grandma gets knocked to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a strong black tea grown in the Indian state of that name.

clue.text: Cartoon strip that's of little worth

definitions.meaning: the long-running comic strip by Charles Schulz featuring Charlie Brown and Snoopy
a trifling sum of money, as in working for next to nothing

explanation.surface: A comic strip is dismissed as worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both the Schulz comic strip and slang for a paltry amount.

clue.text: Chicken given supplements ultimately displays signs of ageing

parts.note: chicken and yellow both mean cowardly

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of supplements

explanation.surface: A chicken given food supplements eventually shows its age.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper, teeth and old photos turn yellowish with age, so to yellow is to show age.

clue.text: Nothing leads this writer, discontented refusnik, to back foreign government

indicators.note: to back means the whole string is read backwards
leads puts nothing at the front of the chain

parts.note: nil means nothing
the setter refers to themself as this writer, giving me

indicators.note: discontented means emptied of contents, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: An unhappy Soviet refusenik is led by nothing but the writer to back a foreign regime.
explanation.walkthrough: NIL ME RK is read backwards. A refusenik was a Soviet citizen refused permission to emigrate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the Moscow citadel housing Russia's government, used to mean that government.

clue.text: Frugal Norm, simple character confronting debts

indicators.note: confronting puts the character face to face with the debts, side by side

parts.note: par is the standard or norm, as in golf
Simple Simon is the nursery-rhyme character
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A thrifty man called Norm, a simple soul, faces up to his debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimonious means extremely unwilling to spend money, stingy or thrifty.
